subject: Post-demo: NemoHealth pilot sizing & GPU recommendation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@nemohealth.com>, Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@nemohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: pilot sizing numbers

Thanks for the time today — great demo and very helpful context on your production constraints. Quick recap from our end and the concrete asks to progress to a short pilot: 

1) Target SLOs you reiterated:
   - P95 tail latency: <= 150 ms for up to 512-token responses (non-streamed)
   - Streaming latency: first-byte <= 50 ms, steady-state token latency to be minimized
   - Availability requirement: 99.95% monthly during business hours

2) Expected workload profile:
   - Baseline: 180 requests/minute (3 rps) average, burst to 1,200 requests/minute (20 rps) for short windows
   - Average response size: ~400 tokens; peak multi-turn sessions up to 2,000 tokens total (KV cache use anticipated)
   - Concurrent streaming sessions target: 30–50 active streams during peak

3) Customer asks for pilot deliverables:
   - A recommended reserved throughput (instances/slots) and GPU shortlist for the pilot
   - A short benchmark plan (what we'll test and metrics we'll collect)
   - A mutual action plan with dates for a 2-week pilot and success criteria

Attachments: attaching a first-pass SLO matrix for your confirmation. [attachment: nemo-slo-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Next actions from Redwood: Ben will propose a concise benchmark plan (latency + streaming + throughput), and I’ll circulate a mutually agreed pilot window and M.A.P. Can you confirm the burst windows (time of day and expected frequency) and whether you need encryption-in-use (HSM) for model keys?

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@nemohealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@nemohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: pilot sizing numbers

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifications inline: 

> P95 tail latency: <= 150 ms for up to 512-token responses
This is what our product team said they can operate against; for longer responses (>512 tokens) we can accept higher p95 but would like you to call out breakpoints.

> Baseline / burst numbers
Our production pattern: baseline is roughly 200 requests/minute with predictable spikes around 11:30–12:30 PST and 18:00–19:00 PST where we see ~10 minute bursts reaching 1,000–1,200 req/min. Spikes are short but frequent (3–4 times per week).

> Streaming concurrency
We should plan for 50 concurrent streams as the worst-case; 30 is the comfortable average. Token rates are ~14 tokens/sec during streaming.

On security: yes, we will need KMS integration for key wrapping (not HSM for pilot, but we will need it after production).

I attached a sanitized sample trace from our staging runs — it’s low-volume but should help you size. [attachment: bench-20270607.log (text/plain)]

If you can propose a pilot config that hits the 150 ms p95 for 512 tokens and demonstrates graceful handling of the 1,200 req/min burst, we’re ready to schedule the two-week pilot next month.

Sara
Director, Product Infrastructure
NemoHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NemoHealth pilot — bench plan + GPU shortlist

Karthik / Marissa — internal note / recommended approach for the pilot based on Sara's clarifications: 

Summary of constraints to validate:
- P95 <= 150 ms for <=512 tokens (non-streaming)
- First-byte streaming <= 50 ms, sustain token latency ~12–18 ms/token
- Handle burst to 1,200 req/min for ~10 minutes windows (3–4x/wk)
- Peak concurrent streams: 50

Benchmark plan (high level):
1) Steady-state latency sweep: 1–5 rps up to 20 rps across 128/256/512 token sizes (measure p50/p95/p99)
2) Burst resilience test: ramp to 20 rps sustained for 10 minutes; measure tail and error rate
3) Streaming soak: 50 concurrent streams at 14 tokens/sec for 15 minutes; measure first-byte and token latency
4) KV cache hit/miss scenarios: test 0%, 50%, 90% cache hit rates

GPU shortlist and rough sizing logic:
- H100 80GB (preferred): best single-card throughput for long contexts and streaming; expect ~3–4 concurrent 512-token non-stream requests per card at target latency when using optimized kernels and int8 quantization + Redwood batching. Estimated reserved slots: 12 slots across 4 H100s to cover burst and headroom.
- A100 80GB: competitive for non-quantized workloads, slightly higher latency for streaming; would need ~6–8 cards to match H100 throughput for this workload.
- L40S: lower cost option; ok for smaller models/shorter contexts but riskier for 2k-turn sessions. Consider only as fallback for cost-constrained pilots.

Suggested pilot config (for 2-week test):
- Start with 4 x H100 (80GB) with 12 reserved concurrency slots, integer-8 quantized model variant, prefix/KV cache enabled.
- Autoscale policy to allow burst to 6 more slots (soft cap) using spare capacity; we’ll monitor queueing and tail latencies.
- Instrumentation: token-level traces, per-slot latency histogram, streamer metrics, and cost telemetry.

Deliverables for Nemo:
- Bench results (CSV + brief summary)
- SLO compliance report vs agreed criteria
- Recommendation for production commit (instances and cost estimate)

I’ll draft the actual bench script (wrk/locust + stream harness) and the Grafana dashboards. Karthik — want me to include an explicit cost delta (H100 vs A100 vs L40S) in the pilot proposal?

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@nemohealth.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@nemohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: pilot sizing numbers

Thanks Sara — useful details. Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

- Week 0 (prep): confirm pilot window (suggested start 2027-07-12), provide service account + staging endpoint details, and share access to sanitized traces (you already attached one)
- Week 1–2 (pilot): Redwood runs benchmarks and streaming soak vs agreed SLOs; daily check-ins Mon/Wed/Fri 30m
- End of Week 2: deliver SLO compliance report and production sizing recommendation + cost estimate

Pilot success criteria (pass):
- P95 <= 150 ms for 512-token responses in steady-state and during a controlled 10-minute burst to 1,200 req/min with error rate <0.5%
- Streaming first-byte <= 50 ms and token latency <= 20 ms/token for 90% of tokens during the soak
- Demonstrated autoscale/fallback behavior with no more than 2x degradation in p95 during unplanned spikes

I’ve added the MAP to our HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890 and created a shared Drive folder for logs and artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NemoPilot

Requested items from Nemo to lock in the pilot:
1) Confirm pilot start date (we suggested 2027-07-12)
2) Confirm you’re OK with Redwood using H100 instances for the pilot (we can swap to A100 if preferred; we’ll include both cost lines)
3) Provide a service account and staging endpoint + any sandbox auth details

If you confirm those three items I’ll circulate a short SOW and our pilot runbook this week.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@nemohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: pilot sizing numbers

All good — we’ll proceed. Quick confirmations: 

1) Pilot start: 2027-07-12 confirmed
2) H100 for pilot: yes, approved (we’ll evaluate cost vs A100 after results)
3) Service account + staging endpoint: infra@nemohealth.com will send the credentials by EOD Friday (10 Jun)

We also want the SOW and pilot runbook before the start date; please include the data handling/retention limits (14 days for logs) and the KMS integration notes (we want key wrapping via AWS KMS; HSM later).

Ben — feel free to proceed with the bench script. Looking forward to seeing the first run.

Sara
Director, Product Infrastructure
NemoHealth
